article_title: Structural Relationships between Environmental Factors, Psychological Health, and Academic Performance in Medical Students Engaged in Online Learning during the COVID-19 Pandemic.
citation: Taleb Ola K., Sarimah Abdullah, Siti-Azrin Ab Hamid, Baharuddin Kamarul Aryffin, Abusafia Ali H. (2023). Structural Relationships between Environmental Factors, Psychological Health, and Academic Performance in Medical Students Engaged in Online Learning during the COVID-19 Pandemic. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph20021494
title: Questionnaire battery: LNT scale, technology scale, and GHQ-12 with verified GPA
description: The study used a three-part online self-administered questionnaire: a 9-item LNT scale covering "lighting, noise, and temperature", a 6-item technology scale measuring adequacy of technology for online classes, and the 12-item GHQ-12 for psychological distress, plus a 9-item proforma for sociodemographics and GPA. GPA was verified with the academic office. In this sample the measurement models showed good fit (e.g., LNT: CFI = 0.99, TLI = 0.98, SRMR = 0.03, RMSEA = 0.03).
requirements: Items were answered on five-point Likert scales, and all questions were compulsory; GPA was verified against academic office records
constraints: The technology scale's upper 90% CI of robust RMSEA was 0.16 in this sample; the study excluded students with a history of underlying psychological issues
target_learners: undergraduate medical students in online learning
target_learning_goals: measuring environmental conditions, psychological health, and academic performance in online learning contexts
examples: Administered via Google Form to 207 second- and third-year medical students at USM, completed in 20–30 minutes
